title: Compatible normalized unit-root lifts of a local DVR diagram
statement:
Let $S\to T$ be an injective local homomorphism of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with compatible fraction fields $N\subseteq F$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $h\geq1$ have invertible image in $S$, and let $u\in S^\times$. There exist finite separable algebraic field extensions $N'/N$ and $F'/F$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], compatible embeddings $N'\hookrightarrow F'$ extending $N\hookrightarrow F$, and $r\in N'$ such that $r^h=u$, $N'=N(r)$ and $F'=F(r)$ (using the image of $r$ in the last equality). Let $D$ and $E$ be the integral closures of $S$ in $N'$ and of $T$ in $F'$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. There exist maximal ideals $a\subset D$, $b\subset E$ with $b\cap D=a$, $a\cap S=\mathfrak m_S$ and $b\cap T=\mathfrak m_T$, such that $S_1=D_a$ and $T_1=E_b$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] are discrete valuation rings and the canonical maps form a commuting square of injective local homomorphisms $S\to S_1$, $T\to T_1$, $S_1\to T_1$, $S\to T$. The element $r$ belongs to $S_1$, and
$$\mathfrak m_SS_1=\mathfrak m_{S_1},\qquad \mathfrak m_TT_1=\mathfrak m_{T_1}.$$
Both residue extensions $S_1/\mathfrak m_{S_1}$ over $S/\mathfrak m_S$ and $T_1/\mathfrak m_{T_1}$ over $T/\mathfrak m_T$ are finite separable. Here $N(r)$ and $F(r)$ mean generated subfields; finite means finite-dimensional; local means pulling back maximal ideals. There is no finiteness or residue-separability assumption on $F/N$.

source.place: Tag 0BRM, lemma-abhyankar, first claim (adjoin an h-th root of a unit), expressed for an arbitrary local DVR diagram with its selected normalization branches.

proof.text: For $R=S,T$, the DVR definition makes $R$ a principal ideal domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], it is Noetherian and integrally closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is integral with function field $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, and its stalk at $p$ is $R_p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] at each prime to see that all these stalks are normal domains. The affine cover consisting of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ itself is a Noetherian affine cover; the spectrum is quasi-compact (indeed a local PID which is not a field has exactly the primes $0$ and $\mathfrak m_R$). Thus both base spectra meet the normal integral Noetherian hypotheses of the component lemma below.

source.place: Tags 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain); Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves). Base hypotheses for the first claim of Tag 0BRM.

proof.text: Put $C=S[X]/(X^h-u)$ and $B=T[X]/(X^h-u)$, with roots $x_C,x_B$ and coefficient map $C\to B$. The image of $h$ is a unit in $T$, since ring maps carry units to units. For either base $R$, the root $x$ is a unit: $x\cdot(u^{-1}x^{h-1})=1$. Hence the derivative $hx^{h-1}$ is a unit. The algebra localized at this derivative is therefore the original root algebra, and [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative] proves it etale. Its root satisfies a monic equation and generates it, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] proves it finite over $R$. It is nonzero: division by the monic degree-$h$ polynomial gives unique representatives of degree less than $h$, and in particular the class of $1$ is nonzero. This calculation applies to $h=1$ as well.

source.place: Tag 0BRM (lemma-abhyankar), first claim, finite etale unit-root algebras; Algebra Tags 00UC (lemma-standard-etale), 02JJ (lemma-characterize-finite-in-terms-of-integral).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-normal-generic-components] to $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ and choose a nonempty component. It is $\operatorname{Spec}E$ for the integral closure $E$ of $T$ in its finite separable generic field $F'$. Its generic algebra is a field quotient of $F[X]/(X^h-u)$, so $F'=F(r)$ for the image $r$ of $x_B$, and $r^h=u$. Inside $F'$ let $N'=N[r]$. It has dimension at most $h$ over $N$ and is a domain. Multiplication by any nonzero element is an injective endomorphism of this finite-dimensional vector space, hence surjective; thus $N'$ is a field and equals $N(r)$. The map $N[X]/(X^h-u)\to N'$ is surjective. Apply the same component lemma to $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}S$: its generic algebra is a finite product of finite separable fields. A surjective map from this product to a field selects one factor (the orthogonal coordinate idempotents map to $0$ or $1$, exactly one to $1$). Consequently $N'/N$ is finite separable, and its selected component is $\operatorname{Spec}D$, where $D$ is the integral closure of $S$ in $N'$. Both $S\to D$ and $T\to E$ are finite etale and their spectra are surjective. The inclusion $N'\subseteq F'$ extends $N\subseteq F$ by construction.

source.place: Tag 0BQL (lemma-finite-etale-covering-normal-unramified), statement and both proof paragraphs; unit-root generic fields in the first claim of Tag 0BRM.

proof.text: The inclusion $N'\hookrightarrow F'$ restricts to an injective $S$-algebra map $D\to E$: every element of $D$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $S$, whose image is a monic polynomial over $T$. The surjection $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ from step 3 gives a prime $b$ above $\mathfrak m_T$. Set $a=b\cap D$. The square of ring inclusions commutes, and locality of $S\to T$ gives $a\cap S=(b\cap T)\cap S=\mathfrak m_S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal], $a$ and $b$ are maximal, applied respectively to the integral maps $S\to D$ and $T\to E$. Here integrality is part of the definition of each integral closure. This selects compatible branches without any algebraicity assumption on $F/N$.

source.place: Tag 0BRM (lemma-abhyankar), first claim, choice of an upper maximal ideal and its lower contraction; Algebra Tag 00GS (lemma-integral-over-field).

proof.text: Set $S_1=D_a$ and $T_1=E_b$. The inclusions into $N'\subseteq F'$ identify these localizations with subrings of these fields. The map $S_1\to T_1$ is $d/s\mapsto d/s$: if $s\notin a$, then its image is not in $b$, so the map is defined and injective. Its maximal ideal contracts to $aD_a$, since $d/s$ lies in $bE_b$ exactly when $d\in a$. The identical fraction calculation proves $S\to S_1$ and $T\to T_1$ injective and local, using $a\cap S=\mathfrak m_S$ and $b\cap T=\mathfrak m_T$. All four maps commute because their values on $S$ agree in $F'$. Finally $r\in D$, since $r^h=u$ is a monic equation over $S$; hence $r\in S_1$.

source.place: Tag 0BRM (lemma-abhyankar), first claim, displayed local square; explicit fraction maps using Algebra Tag 00CO and the local-ring conventions of Tag 07BH.

proof.text: Choose uniformizers $\pi_S,\pi_T$ using the DVR definition. Apply [lem-sbc-etale-trait-stalk] to the finite etale maps $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}T$, at $a$ and $b$. Their images are the closed points by step 4. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], the actual source stalks and structural maps are $D_a=S_1$, $E_b=T_1$ and their canonical maps. The trait-stalk lemma proves these stalks are domain DVRs and gives $\mathfrak m_{S_1}=(\pi_S)$ and $\mathfrak m_{T_1}=(\pi_T)$. These are exactly $\mathfrak m_SS_1=\mathfrak m_{S_1}$ and $\mathfrak m_TT_1=\mathfrak m_{T_1}$, since extending a principal ideal extends its generator.

source.place: Tag 0AP2 (lemma-Dedekind-etale-extension), local DVR assertion; Tag 0BRM first claim; Schemes Tag 01HV for the actual affine stalk maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] to the etale algebra maps $S\to D$ at $a$ and $T\to E$ at $b$. By the contractions in step 4, it gives finite separable extensions $\kappa(a)/\kappa(\mathfrak m_S)$ and $\kappa(b)/\kappa(\mathfrak m_T)$. The localization definition identifies these four fields respectively with $S_1/\mathfrak m_{S_1}$, $S/\mathfrak m_S$, $T_1/\mathfrak m_{T_1}$, $T/\mathfrak m_T$, with the canonical residue maps. This supplies the remaining two clauses. Only invertibility of $h$ and the local inclusion of the original DVRs have been used.

source.place: Tags 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field), 00U4 (lemma-etale-at-prime), and 07BH; finite separable residue extensions in Tag 0BRM, first claim.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BRM (lemma-abhyankar), first claim; normalization of the finite etale root components made explicit by Tag 0BQL, with Tags 00UC, 00U4, 0AP2 and 01HV for the algebra and local assertions.
